answer: Agents must stamp a copper lotus petal onto a horizon clock’s face, the petal’s alloy tarnishing at 3µm per pulse. Any second petal chips away its hour mark in 10ms, zeroing the slot. A Sybil presses extra petals, each costing 10ms plus 3µm of unique alloy—farms can’t mill microns in bulk or reroll the same die more than once.
